Love thy neighbour

By: Graham Coetzer | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
In a democracy with one of the world's most progressive consitutions, we ask whether hate speech is allowed from the pulpit.

Unique Selling Point:
Gay celebrity Somizi Mhlongi recently stormed out of Soweto's Grace Bible Church in protest against a visiting pastor, Bishop Dag Heward-Mills, who referred to homosexuality as "unnatural" during a sermon. Somizi also posted a video to social media, sparking intense debate on the subject. This past sunday members of the LGBTI community held a silent protest at the church's grounds.

Summary:
Our story asks the question: is it hate speech when preached from the pulpit? We have confirmed interviews with Somizi, the spokesperson from the church, Cameron Modisane who organised the protest, Pierre de Vos on the constitutionality and a lawyer from the Human Rights Commission. We will also be speaking to members of the church.

Press Release:


Love thy Neighbour
Religious freedom or the right to self-expression? As gay rights activists call for dialogue at the Grace Bible Church following homophobic references by a guest preacher, Carte Blanche asks: is it hate speech if preached from the pulpit?


Script:


Love thy neighbor
2 Feb 2017

Voice
This is Bishop Dag Heward-Mills preaching at the Grace Bible Church in Soweto 2 weeks ago. The bishop, who is from Ghana, was a guest speaker at the church, but his sermon has the lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and interest or LGBTI community, up in arms because of his reference to homosexuality as “unnatural”.

Sound Up Dag Heward-Mills
You don’t find two male dogs or two male lions, or two male, two male Impalas or two male cats, even lizards, two male elephants. There’s nothing like that in nature, it’s unnatural.

Voice
Gay celebrity Somizi Mhlongo, who has been a member of the church for more than 30 years, left during the sermon and took to Instagram to voice his outrage.

Sound Up Somizi Mhlongo
Gay people must not come to our church. Say it, so that we know, because we go to church to speak to our God whom I believe accepts me for who I am, whom I believe created me the way I am.

Voice
The post caused an outcry on social media, and led to a protest by members of the gay community on church grounds this past Sunday. We caught up with Somizi on the set of his new reality show for an exclusive television interview on the controversy.

Sound Up Somizi
Bongani: In the 32 years that you have been a member, have you ever felt unwelcome in the church in any way?

Somizi: Never, not even once. I think even when I was confused as a teenager with regards to my sexuality, Grace Bible Church was the place where I could feel comfortably easy to accept myself and who I am.

Bongani: So this is like your spiritual home?

Somizi: Yes, definitely, it is my spiritual home.

Voice
Somizi says he found Bishop Heward-Mills’ sermon profoundly hurtful.

Sound Up Dag Heward-Mills
… two male Impalas or two male cats, even lizards, two male elephants. There’s nothing like that in nature, it’s unnatural.

Sound Up Somizi
Somizi: And I deliberately stood up at that time because for me it was like I’m not going to wait and be chicken and wait for a song to start and everybody stands up when they sing so that nobody see’s me, no no no. I was like I’m standing up now for a reason, I’m standing up now whilst you are talking about what doesn’t sit well with me, I’m not going to sit there and cheer with these people. So I’m like let me leave now, because before he carries on and it hurts me more or I become more angry. So I just stood up and left.

Bongani: So when you sat in that service, and heard that message, what were you thinking as you were listening?

Somizi: I don’t have an issue with the scripture. Say it. If the scripture says if a man sleeps with another man like they would sleep with a woman its a sin, talk about it. Say it as it is. Don’t edit it. My problem was the edit. There is no part in the bible that says have you seen a male dog sleeping with a male dog. Now you are perpetuating hate. You are like a person who has raped a lesbian and killed a lesbian, and is in church that day, is like I didn’t do anything bad actually. Look, even this guy agrees with me. That was my issue

Voice
In a statement released by the church’s Bishop Mosa Sono on the29th of January, the church stood its ground on its right to religious freedom

Sound Up Bishop Mosa Sono
As an organization of faith, we believe it is within our constitutional rights to determine our rules and conditions of membership for those who wish to be part of us

Link Bongani
Equality, freedom of religion, of expression, the right to assemble and to picket – these are all enshrined in the constitution. But do some rights trump others?

Voice
We put the question to constitutional law expert Professor Pierre de Vos, who we spoke to from Cape Town via Facetime.

Bongani: So when it comes to religious freedom, surely churches have a right to their beliefs?

Pierre: The Constitutional court has said that you have a right to freedom of religion, which means you have a right to hold a religious belief but also to propagate that religious belief. But it is not an absolute right. Like any right it is limited. For example if your religious belief says that you have to incite violence against a group of people, no court in South Africa is going to say that that is justified because it is religiously inspired.

Sound Up Mosa Sono
We believe and affirm that marriage is an institution created by God, in which one man and one woman enters into an exclusive relationship for life. And that it is the only form of partnership approved by God for sexual relations.

Link Bongani
To be clear, this issue is much broader then just the Grace Bible Church. In many respects it speaks to the faith at large. Because for many believers it all starts and ends with the word of God, the bible.

Voice
The Reverend Teboho Klaas from The Other Foundation, an organization that seeks to advance the rights and social inclusion of people of all sexual orientations and gender identities, says that people who want to take every piece of scripture in the bible literally, should do so in totality.

Sound Up Reverend Teboho Klaas
Bongani: Many churches will say we do know what God’s will is, it’s in the bible. And we can’t change what the bible says. This is the position many churches adopt.

Teboho: There are verses, chapters and verses, that have consequences for what you eat or don’t eat, what you wear or don’t wear. And those verses and chapters happen to be what we don’t talk about now, which essentially is contradicting what the bible says.

Voice
A draft version of a controversial new bill, the Prevention and Combating of Hate Crimes and Hate Speech bill, will criminalize hate speech and could see offenders ending up behind bars. The reverend says it’s time churches and their congregations seek to find God’s will through love and acceptance, rather than marginalization and oppression.

Sound Up Teboho
We in South Africa have emerged from a past of struggle. And it is interesting that those now who are in freedom and democracy do not see that there are struggles of others. You know the struggle of homosexual, bi-sexual and transgender people is a struggle that we need to connect with a struggle of oppression.

Voice
It’s also a struggle against extreme violence, horrific hate crimes such as corrective rape are still all too common in South Africa. One of the organizers of last week’s protest at Grace Bible Church is activist Cameron Modisane, whom says anti-gay messages from the pulpit often lead to atrocities against members of the LBGTI community.

Sound Up Cameron Modisane
The hatred that comes, that we see in terms of the violence that is faced by us as homosexuals, it actually mostly comes from the church. You know people, especially in townships like Soweto and many other townships, you know they act out what the pastor is saying.

Voice
Cameron says the church’s response to their protest, which he argues was aimed to promote dialogue with the church, was heavy handed.

Sound Up Cameron
Cameron: They released their “bouncers”, their security on us, to actually have us removed from their premises…

Bongani: They physically moved you off the premises?

Cameron: Exactly. Precisely. And they actually wanted to manhandle some of the ladies there, but we told them they must not touch any of us, we’ll just walk out peacefully. Because we weren’t fighting, we just wanted to have a peaceful and a silent protest.

Voice
We asked the Grace Bible Church for an on camera interview but they declined, referring us to their statement posted on-line.

Sound Up Bishop Mosa Sono
We believe every human being is created in the image of God, and as such has intrinsic dignity and worth which is why everyone, regardless of their race, gender, sex and amongst others sexual orientation is welcome in our church.

Link Bongani
At the center of this debate is a simple conflict – if churches are uncompromising about scripture as the ultimate authority that binds them, so too is the constitution as the supreme law of the land.

Sound Up Pierre de Vos
In principal all rights have the same status in our law. Of course, given our history, the right to equality is often seen as first among equals among all the rights.

Voice
Gushwell Brooks from the South African Human Rights Commision says the Constitution was designed to protect us all, and that we as South Africans should embrace it.

Sound Up Gushwell
It’s an age-old cliché that we have the best constitution in the world, but that is actually the case. But the question we have to ask ourselves is has it been holistically adopted and accepted by members of ordinary society, by ordinary people.

Link Bongani
So was this a powerful message based on a firm conviction about what is right or wrong, or was it simply hate speech being spewed from the pulpit?

Sound Up Gushwell
You are allowed to believe whatever you want to believe, but in conveying whatever messages you are conveying, are you then committing an act of hate speech? Because remember our freedom of expression is limited, it doesn’t extend to hate speech, when it’s hurtful and harmful.

Voice
The difference between religious freedom and the right to self-expression is a contentious subject, but perhaps one that should be approached from a starting point of love and not hate.

Sound Up Somizi
Bongani: Will you go back?

Somizi: Yes, I will definitely go back, with pride. That church is my church, God is for us all.
